newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.82 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.82 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul stock market index continued on Monday the recent string of records prompted by political optimism ahead of a parliamentary confidence vote in the new right-left coalition government, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at a new all-time high of 1,953, up 35 points, or 1.82 percent from Friday's previous record of 1,918. It had gained 5.67 percent last week and 10.5 percent the previous week, breaking a total of six records.
Trade volume dropped to 27.89 trillion lira ($185.9 million) from Friday's 29.69 trillion lira ($197.6 million).

"The market tested resistance at the index's 1,950 level. It may try the 2,000-point target until the (July 12) confidence vote unless extraordinary political developments come up," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.
"The uptrend will remain intact if liquidity inflow continues," he added.
Turkey's right-left coalition government formed last Monday by conservative Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz will face a confidence vote in parliament on July 12.
Brokers widely expect the government to win the vote and say the market is likely to concentrate on the government's economic performance after the vote.
